turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I suppose you believe your words have changed my opinion of you, but they have not.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I must confess, Elizabeth, that I find it astonishing you continue to harbor such ill will towards me, after all I have done to demonstrate my sincerity.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: You have done nothing to demonstrate your sincerity, Mr. Darcy. Your past behavior speaks for itself, and I will not be swayed by empty words now.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I must confess, Miss Bennet, that I find your rejection most puzzling. Given the circumstances, I would have expected a more gracious acknowledgment of my affections.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I am not puzzled, Mr. Darcy. I am relieved to finally be free from the burden of your unwanted attentions, and I am astonished that you would have the audacity to suggest that I should be grateful for your affections.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I must confess, Miss Bennet, that your words have pained me. I had hoped that my declaration would have met with a more... favorable response.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I am not pained by your declaration, Mr. Darcy. I am not even surprised. My feelings for you are not romantic, and I find your behavior towards me and others to be thoroughly objectionable.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I must confess, Miss Bennet, I am astonished by your audacity in rejecting me after I have so thoroughly demonstrated my devotion to you.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I am astonished, Mr. Darcy, not by my audacity, but by your audacity in thinking that I could ever accept your affections after the way you have treated me and my family.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Your rejection, though anticipated, is not altogether surprising, given the prejudices you hold against me. I had hoped, however, that you would see beyond the mistakes of my past and acknowledge the sincerity of my affections.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I must say, Mr. Darcy, your notion of 'sincerity' is quite amusing, given your history of condescension and manipulation.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I am astonished, Miss Bennet, that you continue to harbor such unfounded animosity towards me, despite the many efforts I have made to improve my behavior and address your misconceptions about my character.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I must confess, Mr. Darcy, that your efforts to improve your behavior seem rather too little, too late. Your past actions have left a lasting impression on me, and I fear that no amount of self-improvement can erase the hurt you have caused.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I am astonished, Miss Bennet, that you should so callously dismiss the sincerity of my feelings, particularly when I have undergone such a radical transformation in my behavior, all for the sake of winning your approval.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I am not some prize to be won, Mr. Darcy. Your transformation, as you call it, is nothing but a desperate attempt to salvage your reputation after the harm you caused me and my family.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I daresay, Elizabeth, you wound me with your words, but I assure you, my intentions are genuine. I have come to realize my past behavior was misguided, and I hope you can find it within yourself to forgive me.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I am not so easily swayed by grand apologies and professions of love, Mr. Darcy. Your past behavior spoke volumes about your character, and I will not be fooled by a change of heart now.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I fail to comprehend, Elizabeth, how you can so obstinately refuse to consider my sincere affections when, by all accounts, I have made amends for past transgressions.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: You expect me to believe that your past behavior was simply a mistake, a misstep, when it was nothing but a series of insulting and hurtful actions towards me and my family?

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I must confess, I find it quite astonishing that you continue to harbor such strong emotions towards me, Elizabeth. Your resentment and dislike are, I dare say, entirely unwarranted, given the circumstances.

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: In vain have I struggled. It will not do. My feelings will not be repressed. You must allow me to tell you how ardently I admire and love you.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: In such cases as this, it is, I believe, the established mode to express a sense of obligation for the sentiments avowed, however unequally they may be returned. It is natural that obligation should be felt, and if I could feel gratitude, I would now thank you. But I cannot--I have never desired your good opinion, and you have certainly bestowed it most unwillingly. I am sorry to have occasioned pain to anyone. It has been most unconsciously done, however, and I hope will be of short duration. The feelings which you tell me have long prevented the acknowledgment of your regard can have little difficulty in overcoming it after this explanation.

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: And this is all the reply which I am to have the honour of expecting! I might, perhaps, wish to be informed why, with so little endeavour at civility, I am thus rejected. But it is of small importance.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: I might as well inquire, why, with so evident a design of offending and insulting me, you chose to tell me that you liked me against your will, against your reason, and even against your character? Was not this some excuse for incivility, if I was uncivil? But I have other provocations. You know I have. Had not my own feelings decided against you, had they been indifferent, or had they even been favourable, do you think that any consideration would tempt me to accept the man who has been the means of ruining, perhaps for ever, the happiness of a most beloved sister?

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: I have every reason in the world to think ill of you. No motive can excuse the unjust and ungenerous part you acted there. You dare not, you cannot deny that you have been the principal, if not the only means of dividing them from each other, of exposing one to the censure of the world for caprice and instability, the other to its derision for disappointed hopes, and involving them both in misery of the acutest kind.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: Can you deny that you have done it?

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: I have no wish of denying that I did everything in my power to separate my friend from your sister, or that I rejoice in my success. Towards him I have been kinder than towards myself.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: But it is not merely this affair, on which my dislike is founded. Long before it had taken place, my opinion of you was decided. Your character was unfolded in the recital which I received many months ago from Mr. Wickham. On this subject, what can you have to say? In what imaginary act of friendship can you here defend yourself? or under what misrepresentation can you here impose upon others?

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: You take an eager interest in that gentleman’s concerns.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: Who that knows what his misfortunes have been can help feeling an interest in him?

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: yes, his misfortunes have been great indeed.
